references.text: Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, are mentioned as the two tribes that were to receive their inheritance, which explains why the lot fell for Joseph's children in chapter 16.
The continuation of the land distribution to Joseph's descendants, specifically the tribe of Manasseh, completing the description of Ephraim's inheritance.
Refers to the house of Joseph receiving two parts, confirming the distribution described in chapter 16.
Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, are mentioned in the census, showing their status as separate tribes in Israel.
Joseph's descendants through Ephraim and Manasseh are assigned leaders for the land distribution, linking to the lot that fell for them.
Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh as his own, providing the basis for them receiving separate inheritance lots.
Jericho is mentioned as an important geographical point, the same place that serves as a reference point for the boundary of Joseph's inheritance.
Describes the border going up to Bethel, the same geographical area mentioned in Joseph's lot at Beth-El.
